newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street shares seen softer at open.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street shares seen softer at open.

text.p: Wall Street shares are expected to open slightly lower on Monday, with wary investors treading gingerly after strong economic data sparked declines in stocks and bonds on Friday.
A rising dollar could also add an element of caution to markets, analysts said.

"After Friday's strong data, markets are defensive," said Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments. "The stronger dollar is also a worry. If banks try to prop up European currencies, it could hurt financial markets."

On Friday, above-forecast gains in July employment, coupled with a strong rise in the National Association of Purchasing Management index, gave new life to old inflation fears and sent markets tumbling.
The Dow Jones Industrial average, which was down as much as 119 points during the session, finished with a loss of 29 points at 8194.

Despite Friday's late-session recovery, markets will start this week on edge, analysts said. There are very few pieces of crucial economic data or earnings reports to give the markets direction, they said.
"We are probably headed for a lower open, simply because of the weaker close on Friday and some softness in European markets," said Hildegard Zagorski of Prudential Securities.
In early trade, the Standard & Poor's 500 futures index was off 1.60 points at 951.40. The long bond, which registered steep losses Friday, was off 2/32 at a 6.46 percent yield.

The dollar surged to a new 94-month high of 1.8730 marks. It was underpinned by the robust U.S. jobs data for July and waning fears that the Bundesbank would raise key money market rates to stem the mark's slide.
But Westfalia's Cardillo said the dollar had become too strong and any action by European central banks to support their currencies could spook bonds and stocks.
"We have to be cautious at these levels, given the stronger dollar," he said.
Among economic data due today are construction spending for June, at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT, which is forecast to rise 1.1 percent compared to a 1.8 percent decline in May.
Japan's Nikkei average closed off 136.31 points, or 0.69 percent, at 19,668.07.
Tokyo stocks were weighed down by growing skepticism over Japan's economic recovery, which prompted profit-taking in leading blue chip issues, traders said.
In London the FTSE 100 was off 2.4 at 4896.9.
U.S. stocks were mixed in London trading.
The Wall Street Journal said in its Heard on the Street column that some analysts think ITT Corp stock has seen its best days.
